📋 Bassin Parisien : anticlinaux peu prof: 📋 Paris Basin: shallow anticlines (600-1300 m), strong post-Variscan exhumation (×2.8), almost no offshore. Lias or Triassic source rock. Good teaching case for paleo-maturation.
📋 Mer du Nord : deux systèmes possibles,: 📋 North Sea: two possible systems, drawn at random each game. In the south, Rotliegend gas sealed by Zechstein salt, with Carboniferous coals as source rock below the reservoir. In the centre, Brent oil whose source rock (Kimmeridge) lies above the reservoir and charges it through faults. Salt halokinesis, normal faults, 90% offshore, high geothermal gradient.
📋 Bassin de rift : failles normales inte: 📋 Rift basin: intense normal faulting, horsts and grabens, strong thermal gradient. High structural diversity. Good reservoirs on horst flanks.
📋 Marge passive : séquences progradantes: 📋 Passive margin: prograding sequences, sedimentary wedge, possible salt (evaporites). Turbidite or shelf carbonate reservoirs.
📋 Bassin d\\'avant-pays : plissement com: 📋 Foreland basin: compressional folding, chevron anticlines, thrusts. Structures are often well defined but depth varies.
📋 Bassin d\\'Aquitaine : profondeurs mod: 📋 Aquitaine Basin: moderate depths (1300-2600 m), faults and folds linked to the Pyrenean orogeny, localized Triassic salt. Mostly onshore with an offshore fringe (Parentis type). A good intermediate case between Paris and the North Sea.
📋 Gulf Coast : bassin cénozoïque très su: 📋 Gulf Coast: highly subsiding Cenozoic basin (2200-5000 m), intense salt tectonics (Louann salt), growth faults, almost no exhumation (basin still subsiding, not uplifted). Mostly offshore. Teaching case for the difference between continuous subsidence and exhumation.
